papers.title: Certified Multi-Turn Robustness for LLM Safety via Compositional Bounds and Safety Persistence
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are vulnerable to multi-turn jailbreak attacks that progressively manipulate conversation context. Existing certified robustness methods are limited to single-turn inputs; naive multi-turn composition yields bounds that degrade exponentially in the number of turns. We introduce Multi-Turn Certified Robustness (MTCR), a framework that models conversational safety via State-Adversarial MDPs and defines $k$-turn certified robustness as the worst-case safety probability across $k$ adversarial turns. MTCR comprises: (i) compositional certification via embedding-space mode decomposition, yielding tighter certified lower bounds than naive multiplication; (ii) $(α,β)$-safety persistence, improving the degradation rate from $\underline{p}^{k}$ to $β^k$ (with $β> \underline{p}$) and yielding interpretable horizon estimates; (iii) matching information-theoretic upper bounds establishing tightness; and (iv) a unified algorithm combining these results. Experiments on six LLMs under $ε$-bounded and Crescendo-style attacks confirm that empirical safety consistently exceeds the certified bounds.

summary.evidence: 实验在六种LLM上验证，显示实证安全超过认证界限，但未提供具体数值。
summary.limitations: 未在摘要中提及具体限制。
summary.method: 作者通过状态对抗MDP建模对话安全，并提出组合认证和(α,β)-安全持续性机制。
summary.problem: 现有方法无法处理多轮越狱攻击，导致认证界限随轮数指数级退化。
summary.takeaway: MTCR框架通过组合认证和安全持续性机制，实现了比传统方法更优的多轮鲁棒性认证。
summary.why_for_you: 高效对抗训练中的多轮鲁棒性认证问题。

papers.title: FL-MAESTRO: Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration for Resource-Constrained Federated Learning
papers.abstract: In Federated Learning (FL), the communication topology is a runtime variable rather than a fixed design choice, since links and edge devices drop in and out during training. Each round, the server must commit three coupled decisions, namely the communication topology, per-client resource allocation, and the aggregation rule for combining local updates. Recent agentic systems have begun bringing large language models (LLM) into FL, but the existing line of work either operates at setup time or handles a single runtime dimension such as client selection. We propose FL-MAESTRO, a multi-agent orchestrator that makes the joint runtime FL decision directly through three specialist LLM agents, one per decision dimension. A coordinator combines their analyses into a single decision, and a non-LLM feasibility check confirms it before the round executes. Because the orchestrator consumes the server's predicted-failure list, it withholds clients whose updates would never be aggregated, which removes the dominant source of wasted round energy in classical FL on volatile edge networks. Because client state is read as natural-text profiles, the same orchestrator extends to heterogeneous device classes without per-class energy models. On a non-IID CIFAR-10 benchmark, FL-MAESTRO matches the accuracy of the strongest energy-aware baseline while cutting wasted round energy from over a third to near zero. Code is available at https://github.com/denoslab/FL-MAESTRO.

summary.takeaway: FL-MAESTRO uses three specialist LLM agents to jointly decide topology, resources, and aggregation each FL round, eliminating most wasted energy.
summary.problem: Federated learning suffers from wasted round energy due to volatile client availability and fixed topology/resource decisions.
summary.method: A multi-agent orchestrator employs a TopologyAgent, ResourceAgent, and AggregationAgent whose outputs are synthesized by an LLM coordinator and validated by a non-LLM feasibility check.
summary.evidence: On non-IID CIFAR-10 with 30 clients, FL-MAESTRO reduces wasted round energy from >33% to near zero while matching the strongest energy-aware baseline’s accuracy.
summary.limitations: Evaluation is limited to simulated CIFAR-10 scenarios and does not assess real-world deployments or larger model scales.
summary.why_for_you: If you seek efficient adversarial training, the paper’s resource-aware LLM orchestration may inspire low-energy FL strategies.

signals.text: FL‑MAESTRO jointly orchestrates topology, per‑client resources, and aggregation each round via three specialist LLM agents.
Coordinator synthesizes agents’ analyses into a feasible joint decision, iterating up to Dmax ∈ {2, 3} and validated by a non‑LLM feasibility check.
On non‑IID CIFAR‑10, FL‑MAESTRO cuts wasted round energy from >33% to near zero while preserving baseline accuracy.

deep_dive.overview: FL-MAESTRO introduces a runtime orchestrator for federated learning that couples three decision dimensions—communication topology, per-client resource allocation, and aggregation weighting—through specialist LLM agents. Each agent reasons over natural‑text client profiles and domain tools, then a central LLM coordinator merges their proposals into a joint decision that a non‑LLM validator enforces for feasibility. In simulated non‑IID CIFAR‑10 experiments with heterogeneous edge clients, the system eliminates most wasted energy without sacrificing model accuracy, demonstrating the practicality of open‑weight LLMs for on‑premise FL control.

methodology.title: Specialist LLM agents
methodology.detail: TopologyAgent, ResourceAgent, and AggregationAgent each receive typed constraint analyses and query tools for communication cost, energy cost, label diversity, and battery feasibility.

methodology.title: Coordinator and Validator
methodology.detail: A synthesis‑only LLM prompt combines the three analyses into a JSON decision (C+, τ, {ri}, σ); a Python validator enforces battery eligibility, aggregator capability, weight normalization, and clipping of infeasible values.

methodology.title: Collaboration protocol
methodology.detail: Agents iterate up to Dmax ∈ {2, 3} times, revising proposals after seeing the other dimensions to enforce coupling before final synthesis.

mechanism.title: Predicted‑failure filtering
mechanism.detail: The orchestrator consumes the server’s predicted‑failure list, withholding low‑battery clients whose updates would be dropped, thereby removing the dominant source of wasted round energy.

mechanism.title: Natural‑text client profiles
mechanism.detail: Client state is encoded as textual profiles, allowing the same LLM orchestration to handle heterogeneous device classes without per‑class energy models.

mechanism.title: Feasibility clipping
mechanism.detail: Infeasible joint decisions are clipped to feasibility boundaries by the validator, turning LLM errors into repairs rather than runtime crashes.

experiments.title: Setup
experiments.detail: CIFAR‑10 with Dirichlet non‑IID partitions (α = 0.1, 0.3), CNN (545k parameters), 30 clients, battery ∈[0.5,0.9] (hard/ extreme low‑battery subsets), bandwidth bimodal, compute sampled from exp distribution.

experiments.title: Scenarios and baselines
experiments.detail: Two heterogeneous edge scenarios (hard α=0.3, extreme α=0.1) compared against the strongest energy‑aware baseline (e.g., Oort) and classical FL methods (FedAvg, FedProx).

experiments.title: Metrics
experiments.detail: Model accuracy, wasted round energy (percentage of energy spent on clients that drop out before aggregation), and feasibility violation rates.

findings.title: Energy efficiency
findings.detail: FL‑MAESTRO reduces wasted round energy from over a third to near zero across both hard and extreme scenarios.

findings.title: Accuracy preservation
findings.detail: The method matches the accuracy of the strongest energy‑aware baseline despite aggressive client withholding.

findings.title: Feasibility enforcement
findings.detail: The non‑LLM validator successfully clips infeasible decisions, preventing runtime crashes and maintaining stable training.

contributions: Joint runtime FL decision making with multi‑agent LLMs
Energy‑aware orchestration that eliminates wasted round energy
Open‑weight LLM implementation removing cloud dependency
limitations: Only simulated CIFAR‑10 experiments; no real‑world edge deployment
Evaluation limited to a single model size and 30 clients
No analysis of LLM loss‑landscape behavior or adversarial robustness
open_questions: How does multi‑agent LLM orchestration affect loss‑landscape dynamics in federated training?
Can the approach be extended to efficient adversarial training under resource constraints?
What scalability challenges arise when increasing client count and model size beyond the presented experiments?

papers.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment
papers.abstract: Improving the safety of large language models (LLMs) often comes at the expense of utility, as globally applied safety tuning may affect model responses to both harmful and benign inputs. We propose \textbf{C}ontinuous \textbf{L}at\textbf{E}nt \textbf{A}dapter \textbf{R}outing (CLEAR), a conditional safety adaptation framework that uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to continuously control the activation strength of a safety low-rank adapter. CLEAR aims to reduce harmful completions while avoiding unnecessary changes to the frozen backbone that could degrade performance on benign prompts. Experiments on widely used safety and utility benchmarks show that CLEAR improves robustness on HarmBench while reducing the utility degradation observed with globally applied safety tuning such as SFT or standard low-rank adaptation (LoRA). On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, CLEAR reduces HarmBench ASR from 32.3\% to 0.5\%, while retaining most of the base model's utility and achieving up to 7.1 percentage points higher GSM8K accuracy than globally applied SFT or LoRA. These results suggest that CLEAR is a promising mechanism for improving the safety--utility trade-off in LLM alignment.

summary.evidence: 在HarmBench上提升鲁棒性，Llama-3-8B-Instruct的ASR从32.3%降至0.5%，GSM8K准确率比全局SFT或LoRA高7.1个百分点。
summary.method: 使用轻量级隐状态门控连续调节安全低秩适配器的激活强度。
summary.problem: 大型语言模型的安全调优常导致效用下降，需平衡安全与效用。
summary.takeaway: CLEAR通过连续潜变量适配器路由实现安全对齐，同时保持模型效用。
summary.why_for_you: 安全-效用权衡问题的高效对抗训练机制

papers.title: Enforcing LLM Safety through DMD-based Classification of Prompt-Response Embedding Dynamics
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in high-stakes applications, yet their tendency to generate toxic, harmful, or policy-violating content poses significant risks. Detecting these unsafe outputs efficiently in a black-box manner remains an open challenge. In this paper, we extend a recently proposed dynamical systems framework designed for hallucination detection to LLM safety classification. By projecting both prompts and responses into high-dimensional embedding spaces and fitting separate Koopman-based predictive models for safe and unsafe regimes, we classify new outputs using a new differential residual score that compares prediction errors of the safe and unsafe regimes. A key contribution is the incorporation of the prompt and response embedding dynamics, yielding fitted Koopman operators that capture crucial interaction patterns. We evaluate our black-box method across three safety benchmarks using three embedding models. Our results show that incorporating prompt embeddings yields consistent improvements, particularly for interaction-dependent violations when paired with causal decoders (e.g., in Llama-3), while response-only violations benefit more from dense semantic embedding representations. These findings opens the door for using dynamical systems to analyze AI systems rather than the dominant paradigm of using AI to model dynamical systems.

summary.takeaway: 使用 DMD 与 Koopman 算子对提示‑响应嵌入动力学进行分类，可在黑盒条件下提升 LLM 安全检测。
summary.problem: 需要一种无需访问模型内部或多次采样即可高效识别 LLM 有害输出的方法。
summary.method: 将提示和响应的 token 嵌入投射至高维空间，分别拟合安全与不安全的 Koopman 预测模型，利用差分残差分数进行二分类。
summary.evidence: 在三个安全基准上，加入提示嵌入始终提升检测效果，尤其对 Llama‑3 的交互依赖违规有显著增益。
summary.limitations: 仅评估二分类且缺乏多类危害实验和理论可分性保证。
summary.why_for_you: 对可信 LLM 研究者，这提供了无需内部访问的后部署安全监控方案，适合实际部署场景。

signals.text: 首次将提示嵌入动力学加入 Koopman 分类，实现交互依赖安全检测提升。
基于扩展 DMD 拟合安全/不安全 Koopman 算子，比较预测误差得到差分残差分数。
在三项安全基准上，加入提示嵌入对 Llama‑3 的交互违规检测提升显著。

deep_dive.overview: 本文将 LLM 的 token 生成视为离散动力系统，利用扩展 DMD 拟合安全与不安全两套 Koopman 算子，并引入提示嵌入动力学以捕获交互依赖的违规模式。通过差分残差分数实现黑盒二分类，在三个安全基准和三种不同规模的嵌入模型上验证了方法的有效性，揭示了嵌入模型与违规类型之间的细微关系。

methodology.title: 嵌入投射
methodology.detail: 使用 Qwen3-Embed、Mistral、Llama‑3 等预训练模型将提示和响应的 token 转换为高维向量序列。

methodology.title: Koopman 拟合
methodology.detail: 采用扩展 DMD（EDMD）对安全和不安全的嵌入轨迹分别进行最小二乘拟合，得到四个有限维 Koopman 算子。

methodology.title: 差分残差评分
methodology.detail: 在推理阶段计算安全与不安全模型的预测误差差异，作为二分类的决策分数。

mechanism.title: 动力学视角
mechanism.detail: 将 token 嵌入视为可观测的状态轨迹，安全与不安全行为对应不同的动力学流形。

mechanism.title: 交互捕获
mechanism.detail: 通过同时建模提示和响应的 Koopman 算子，捕获仅在两者交互时出现的违规模式。

experiments.title: 基准与模型
experiments.detail: 在三个公开安全基准上评估，使用三种嵌入模型（Qwen3-Embed 0.6B、Mistral 7.2B、Llama‑3 8.0B），采用二分类准确率等指标。

findings.title: 提示嵌入提升
findings.detail: 加入提示嵌入后，所有基准均出现一致的检测性能提升，尤其在交互依赖违规上对 Llama‑3 提升最明显。

findings.title: 模型‑违规匹配
findings.detail: 因果解码器（Llama‑3）适合捕获交互违规，紧凑语义编码器（Qwen‑Embed）更擅长检测仅响应中的不安全内容。

contributions: 提出 Prompt‑aware Koopman 分类框架用于 LLM 安全检测
展示嵌入模型与违规类型之间的细粒度匹配关系
实现无需内部访问或多次采样的黑盒安全监控
limitations: 仅实现二分类（安全/不安全），未覆盖多类别危害标签
实验局限于三种嵌入模型和特定安全基准，缺乏更广泛的评估
未提供安全可分性的理论保证
open_questions: 如何将方法扩展到多类别安全标签（如暴力、仇恨、误导等）？
是否能建立 Koopman 动力学下安全/不安全轨迹可分性的理论界限？
在实时大规模部署环境中，计算开销与响应延迟如何进一步优化？

papers.title: Thermo-FL: Thermal-Aware Robust Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Edge AI
papers.abstract: Federated fine-tuning enables large language models to adapt on edge devices without centralizing private data, but practical deployments must address hardware instability and adversarial update corruption together. Thermally constrained clients may throttle, slow local training, or delay synchronous aggregation, while Byzantine clients and communication-layer adversaries can corrupt the updates used to form the global model. To address these challenges, we present Thermo-FL, a thermal-aware federated LoRA fine-tuning framework that uses device temperature as an active control signal for local adapter training and sparse update transmission. On the client side, Thermo-FL adjusts the active LoRA-layer fraction and transmitted update density as devices heat or cool, reducing workload under thermal stress. On the server side, Thermo-FL introduces TERRA, a robust aggregation pipeline for dynamically sparse LoRA updates that combines norm filtering, mask-aware directional validation, adaptive active-coordinate clipping, and mask-aware aggregation. We evaluate Thermo-FL using both a large-scale emulator and a Jetson-based physical testbed. In the emulator, Thermo-FL improves robustness under adversarial sparse aggregation and achieves the strongest BoolQ accuracy across clean and attack settings while remaining competitive on GSM8K. In the physical prototype, Thermo-FL stabilizes device temperature, reduces compressed upload size through bitmap sparse encoding, and preserves GSM8K utility under sign-flip/scale and MITM perturbations. These results show that secure edge LLM adaptation should jointly consider hardware behavior, workload regulation, sparse communication, and aggregation robustness.

summary.takeaway: Thermal-aware client adaptation combined with robust sparse aggregation enables resilient edge LLM fine‑tuning under thermal stress and adversarial updates.
summary.problem: Edge federated fine‑tuning must simultaneously handle device thermal constraints and malicious update corruption.
summary.method: Thermo‑FL uses device temperature to modulate LoRA layer participation and update sparsity, and introduces TERRA aggregation with norm filtering, mask‑aware directional validation, adaptive clipping, and mask‑aware aggregation.
summary.evidence: In an 80‑client emulator, Thermo‑FL achieved the highest BoolQ exact‑match accuracy (72.32% clean) and improved GSM8K robustness versus sparse FedAvg.
summary.limitations: Evaluation uses only two Jetson clients physically and limited attack scenarios; temperature policy is fixed and device‑specific.
summary.why_for_you: Matches your interest in efficient adversarial training by jointly reducing compute/communication load and defending against update attacks.

signals.text: Thermo-FL integrates temperature-driven LoRA sparsity control with TERRA robust aggregation, achieving top BoolQ accuracy (72.32% clean).
Thermo-FL adjusts LoRA-layer fraction and update density by temperature, while TERRA applies norm filtering and mask-aware directional validation.
Emulator shows Thermo-FL raises FedAvg accuracy from 26.69% to 31.09% under sign‑flip attacks, yet physical tests use only two clients.

deep_dive.overview: Thermo-FL addresses the dual challenge of thermal instability and adversarial updates in edge federated LLM fine‑tuning. Clients monitor device temperature and dynamically reduce the fraction of LoRA layers trained and the sparsity of transmitted updates, easing compute and bandwidth under heat stress. The server employs TERRA, a multi‑stage robust aggregator that filters by norm, validates direction with mask awareness, clips active coordinates adaptively, and aggregates sparsely. Experiments on an 80‑client emulator and a two‑Jetson testbed show superior BoolQ accuracy and improved GSM8K robustness, while also stabilizing temperature and shrinking upload size.

methodology.title: Temperature‑Driven LoRA Control
methodology.detail: Device temperature triggers a policy that lowers the active LoRA‑layer fraction and the top‑k sparsification rate when T ≥ T_crit, reducing local compute and communication.

methodology.title: TERRA Robust Aggregation
methodology.detail: Server‑side pipeline combines norm filtering, mask‑aware directional validation, adaptive active‑coordinate clipping, and mask‑aware aggregation for dynamically sparse updates.

mechanism.title: Thermal Threshold Policy
mechanism.detail: A fixed temperature threshold T_crit and hardware‑specific parameters κ, ρ determine when to switch from full‑frequency (f_max) to throttled frequency (f_th) and adjust LoRA activity.

mechanism.title: Mask‑Aware Directional Validation
mechanism.detail: Updates are accepted only if the cosine similarity of their support‑restricted vectors exceeds a directional threshold τ_dir, rejecting sign‑flipped or misaligned updates.

mechanism.title: Adaptive Coordinate Clipping
mechanism.detail: For surviving updates, each coordinate is clipped to a bound m_{k,j}·q_t, ensuring that at most ρ_max·d coordinates dominate the aggregation.

experiments.title: Large‑Scale Emulator
experiments.detail: 80 logical clients (10 per round, 12.5% participation) fine‑tune Qwen2.5‑0.5B on BoolQ and GSM8K using LoRA rank 16; attacks include sign‑flip and mixed poisoning; metrics: exact‑match accuracy.

experiments.title: Physical Jetson Testbed
experiments.detail: Two Jetson Orin Nano clients and a laptop server evaluate temperature stabilization, bitmap sparse encoding compression, and robustness against sign‑flip/scale and MITM noise attacks.

findings.title: Superior BoolQ Performance
findings.detail: Thermo-FL achieved 72.32% clean, 71.16% sign‑flip, and 72.11% mixed attack accuracy, outperforming all baselines.

findings.title: GSM8K Robustness
findings.detail: Thermo-FL remained competitive (33.74% clean) and improved over sparse FedAvg under attacks (31.09% sign‑flip, 31.67% mixed).

findings.title: System Benefits
findings.detail: Physical prototype showed stabilized device temperature, reduced upload size via bitmap sparse encoding, and preserved utility under adversarial perturbations.

contributions: Thermal‑aware client control that modulates LoRA training and sparsity based on temperature.
TERRA aggregation pipeline integrating norm filtering, mask‑aware directional validation, adaptive clipping, and mask‑aware aggregation.
Empirical demonstration of joint hardware‑aware and robust federated fine‑tuning on LLMs.
limitations: Physical testbed limited to two Jetson clients, not reflecting large‑scale deployments.
Attack evaluation on hardware covered only one sign‑flip/scale and one MITM noise injection scenario.
Temperature control uses fixed thresholds and device‑specific parameters, requiring recalibration for other hardware.
TERRA does not replace cryptographic transport protection or secure boot mechanisms.
open_questions: How can temperature thresholds and adaptation parameters be learned automatically for heterogeneous devices?
Can Thermo-FL scale to dozens or hundreds of diverse edge clients while maintaining robustness?
What is the impact of Thermo-FL on other LLM tasks beyond BoolQ and GSM8K?
How does Thermo-FL interact with secure aggregation or differential privacy mechanisms?

papers.title: Target-Aware Calibration Data Selection for Preserving Uncertainty in Quantized Language Models
papers.abstract: Quantization is widely used to deploy large language models, but its effect on uncertainty behavior, such as confidence, margins, and abstention, is rarely treated as a primary objective. We frame calibration-data selection for quantization as a target-dependent uncertainty-preservation problem. Different deployments emphasize different regions of the input distribution, yet prior work mainly optimizes accuracy-oriented compression metrics or adjusts scores after quantization. We formalize this goal with distributional and boundary preservation risks, and provide a simple mixture-mismatch argument explaining why no single calibration recipe should be expected to fit all targets. We introduce Doubt-Preserving Quantization (DPQ), a lightweight pre-quantization recipe family that uses full-precision predictions to construct target-aligned calibration mixtures of high-doubt examples and generic anchors. Across 8 language models, 9 NLP benchmarks, and 22 comparison methods, the leading fixed recipe changes with the preservation target: DPQ-r75 leads on SQuAD2 answerability-boundary preservation, while milder or single-signal variants, including DPQ-r50, confidence-only, and entropy-only, better preserve broad multiple-choice QA behavior. These results show that calibration data should be selected for the specific full-precision score behavior a deployment needs to preserve, rather than treated as a fixed quantization detail.
papers.comment: 20 pages, 5 figures. Accepted to EMNLP Findings 2026

summary.takeaway: DPQ 通过调整校准数据，保持量化 LLM 中的目标特定不确定性指标。
summary.method: DPQ 利用全精度预测，挑选高疑问样本和通用锚点，构建目标对齐的校准混合。
summary.limitations: 校准数据的选择仍依赖目标，需要针对不同部署优先级重新配置。
summary.evidence: DPQ 变体在 8 种模型和 9 项 NLP 基准上超越 22 种基线，DPQ-r75 在 SQ UAD2 上表现突出，较温和的变体在 MCQA 上表现良好。
summary.why_for_you: 通过自适应校准展示目标感知的不确定性保持，契合您对可信 LLM 数据选择的关注。
summary.problem: 量化常导致不确定性指标（如 confidence margins 和 answerability）下降，若缺乏目标特定校准。

signals.text: DPQ 通过 mixture-mismatch 论证实现不确定性保持。
基于疑问的选择使用 1−p0,(1)−p0,(2) 优先低 margin 示例。
DPQ-r75 在 SQ UAD2 上超越 22 种基线，DPQ-r50 在 MCQA 上表现出色。

deep_dive.overview: 本文通过将校准数据选择形式化为目标依赖问题，解决量化 LLM 中的不确定性退化。DPQ 使用全精度预测构建校准混合，优先高疑问样本和通用锚点。8 种模型、9 项基准的实验显示目标特定的性能提升，DPQ-r75 在 answerability-boundary 任务上表现突出，较温和的变体在广泛 QA 任务上表现良好。该方法不修改 quantizer 参数，而是侧重校准数据的组成。

methodology.detail: 形式化目标依赖的不确定性保持为分布式和边界风险最小化，认为没有单一的校准方案能满足所有部署需求。
methodology.title: Mixture-mismatch framework

methodology.detail: 将可回答的 QA 示例 (ARC-Challenge) 与 SQ UAD2 边界案例相结合，平衡可回答/不可回答样本以进行目标特定训练。
methodology.title: 校准池构建

methodology.detail: 使用确定性过程选择前 ⌊sr⌋ 个高疑惑候选，并用来自 WikiText/RandomQA 的通用锚点填补剩余名额。
methodology.title: 固定预算选择

mechanism.detail: 定义 b(x) = 1−p0,(1)−p0,(2) 用于识别低边际示例，隔离脆弱区域以进行针对性校准。
mechanism.title: 疑惑分数公式

mechanism.detail: 评估将 b(x) 替换为 confidence、entropy 或 answerability 指标的变体，以剥离选择信号的影响。
mechanism.title: 信号隔离实验

experiments.detail: 8 个语言模型（Qwen、Llama、Mistral）在 9 项 NLP 任务（SQ UAD2、ARC-Challenge、OpenBookQA）上进行实验，使用 22 种对比方法，包括 GPTQ、BNB-NF4 和后置校准。
experiments.title: 模型与基准覆盖

experiments.detail: 固定 4 位量化，使用 128 个校准样本，依据 FP 预测进行选择，且不修改量化器参数。
experiments.title: 校准设置

experiments.detail: 包括 accuracy、ECE、NLL、Brier score，以及针对 answerability（SQ UAD2）和 distributional preservation（MCQA）的任务特定度量。
experiments.title: 评估指标

findings.detail: DPQ-r75 在 SQ UAD2 上达到 80.6% accuracy，较 FP 的 84.7%；DPQ-r50 达到 79.2% 对比 FP 的 83.3%，展示了校准适配能力。
findings.title: 目标特定性能

findings.detail: DPQ 变体在保持 confidence margins 方面优于基线，在 SQ UAD2 上的 ECE 为 62.5%，而 BNB-NF4 为 66.7%。
findings.title: 不确定性保持

findings.detail: DPQ 不需要更改量化器，仅重新配置校准数据，且不增加推理成本。
findings.title: 轻量级适配

papers.title: aiXamine: Unified Black-Box Evaluation of Cross-Dimensional Trade-offs in LLM Safety, Security, and Privacy
papers.abstract: The critical failure modes in deployed large language models (LLMs) are cross-dimensional: a model can score 99.3 in safety alignment while refusing one in three benign queries, or improve across every capability metric while losing 21 points in privacy. Existing evaluation frameworks that assess safety, security, and privacy independently cannot detect these patterns. We introduce aiXamine, a unified black-box platform that evaluates LLM trustworthiness across safety, security, and privacy as interdependent properties. aiXamine orchestrates 46 tests across nine services through an automated red-teaming pipeline, producing hierarchical risk profiles, from prompt-level diagnostics to cross-service trade-off analytics, that enable reproducible comparison of proprietary and open-weight systems under identical conditions. Applying aiXamine to over 120 LLMs through more than 5,000 test runs, we conduct the largest joint safety, security, and privacy study to date and uncover three cross-dimensional phenomena invisible to single-axis evaluation. First, safety enforcement incurs a quantifiable safety tax: stronger alignment systematically increases over-refusal, forcing providers to choose between protection and utility. Second, privacy is near-orthogonal to other trustworthiness dimensions and not captured by standard alignment. Third, we identify and formally characterize distillation-induced robustness collapse: off-policy distillation without on-policy correction causes entropy collapse, catastrophically destroying robustness (56.9$\to$2.6) on the same base architecture. These findings, compounded by diminishing returns from scale and category-dependent safety behaviors, demonstrate that trustworthiness is inherently multi-dimensional: progress along one axis does not guarantee, and can actively undermine, progress along others, yet current alignment methods treat it as a single objective.

papers.title: Jacobian-guided Noise Injection for Quantization Robustness in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Quantization of Large Language Models (LLMs) is often hindered by the sensitivity of the self-attention mechanism to discretization errors. We identify the softmax operator as a bottleneck for quantization stability due to its sensitivity to outliers and state-dependent Jacobian. We theoretically establish that suppressing the norm of this Jacobian helps in bounding quantization-induced performance degradation. Based on this, we propose Jacobian-Guided Noise Injection, a training strategy that injects zero-mean Gaussian noise into pre-attention logits, with variance derived directly from the Jacobian Frobenius norm. Unlike prior approaches that rely on heuristic or penalise jacobian directly, our method provides a way to identify the optimal noise variance based on the local attention sensitivity. We evaluate the method on SOTA LLM architectures, where it demonstrates improved robustness over popular PTQ methods. Empirical analysis reveals that the proposed method gives up to +37% relative gains on Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K for SigLIP and improves relative perplexity by upto 40% on WikiText for language models in low bit quantisation settings, proving the efficacy of the approach.

papers.title: PromptResponse: Optimizing Prompts for LLM Coding Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in research workflows and software development pipelines, yet their output remains sensitive to input prompt variations. This paper presents $\unicode{x00AB}$PromptResponse$\unicode{x00BB}$, a controlled study examining how formatting and LLM-based tuning of coding task prompts affect the resulting code's performance, efficiency, and stability. Using five semantically identical yet syntactically distinct variants of the HumanEval dataset$\unicode{x2014}$baseline, JSON, Markdown, YAML, and an LLM-tuned version$\unicode{x2014}$we had GPT-4o solve its coding problems over 8200$\unicode{x00A0}$executions. Our results show that consistent formatting$\unicode{x2014}$especially JSON$\unicode{x2014}$improves generation efficiency and syntactic stability, with minor gains in task performance. Conversely, the LLM-tuned prompts resulted in significantly degraded task performance without significant improvements in any other dimension. These findings suggest that low-effort reformatting alone can yield measurable improvements, while tuning must account for model alignment. We conclude our work with providing a set of practical recommendations informed by our results as well as releasing our dataset variants and evaluation pipeline for future work.

papers.title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
papers.abstract: Mid-training is increasingly recognized as a critical stage for shaping the capabilities of large language models. Recent work has shown that targeted mid-training can strengthen reasoning-intensive abilities such as math and science, and can also improve agentic capabilities in software-engineering settings. In this work, we study the parallel but less explored agentic capability: general tool use. We present MidTool, an open corpus construction pipeline for agentic tool-use mid-training that combines large-scale web, PDF, and code data with synthesized supervision from real-world tool APIs, MCP skills, and document-grounded workflows. MidTool is designed to teach models how to recognize tool affordances, ground arguments from context, compose tool call workflow, and recover from incomplete information. We mid-train Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base on MidTool-Mix, and then apply follow-up post-training with both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Compared with baselines, MidTool-Mix consistently improves downstream performance under both SFT and RL on BFCL, tau2-Bench, and MCP Universe. These results suggest that general tool use, like other important LLM capabilities, benefits from dedicated mid-training rather than being left entirely to post-training.

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Hallucinate Electric Fata Morganas?
papers.abstract: AI hallucinations - that is, outputs which are made up, cannot be verified, or contradict the source material - are generally regarded as an engineering flaw to be dealt with. This paper contends that they also have philosophical significance when it comes to the question of machine consciousness. We examine the known causes of hallucinations in large language models - such as source-target divergence, discrepancies between training and inference, and overfitting - and we present two empirical investigations. In the first, we apply successive generations of the GPT model to ambiguous factual questions under different temperature settings, finding that higher temperatures result in plausible but incorrect answers while lower temperatures lead to factually accurate ones. The sampling parameters that cause a model to seem creative or spontaneous and thus more likely to pass behavioral tests of intelligence are the same ones that increase its hallucination rate. In the second, we look at an encoder-only model that has been trained on encyclopedic data and which answers questions of the same type factually and without embellishment, indicating that hallucinations are due to exposure to subjective and socially diverse training data rather than to the development of any cognitive ability. Using references to Turing, Searle's Chinese Room, the frame problem, and the cybernetic tradition of Wiener and Ashby, we claim that a model's self-reports of emotion or sentience come within the definition of hallucination, and that any future occurrence of machine consciousness might remain epistemically inaccessible since it would be indistinguishable from a sufficiently advanced hallucination.

papers.title: Every Coin Has Two Sides: On the Dual Nature of Generalization in On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher capabilities by supervising trajectories sampled from the student's own policy, yet its generalization behavior remains poorly understood, as most studies evaluate OPD on a single domain and on benchmarks close to the training data. We present a controlled study that varies one generalization factor at a time, from in-domain distribution shifts to cross-domain transfer and the multi-teacher setting. We find that OPD transfers a teacher's reasoning behavior rather than its answers to particular problems: training difficulty barely matters, and even problems the teacher never solves are useful. Transfer depends strongly on the origin relationship between teacher and student: same-origin pairs bring the student close to the teacher across languages, reasoning horizons, and even other domains, whereas cross-origin pairs mostly fit the trained distribution. This broad reach is a double-edged sword: since routing prompts to domain experts cannot confine each teacher's influence, combining them yields a mixture-dependent seesaw among their capabilities. These results clarify when OPD generalizes and offer a useful perspective for diagnosing multi-teacher OPD.

summary.takeaway: OPD主要传递教师的推理模式，而非具体答案，且同源教师在跨语言、跨任务上均能提升学生。

deep_dive.overview: 本文在受控实验框架下系统考察了On‑policy Distillation (OPD) 的多维泛化行为。通过逐一改变训练难度、语言、推理跨度、任务域以及模型来源，发现OPD更倾向于迁移教师的推理模式而非具体答案；同源教师‑学生配对在跨语言、跨任务上均能显著提升学生性能，而跨源配对的跨域收益有限。进一步的多教师实验揭示，教师影响并非局限于路由的领域，混合比例会导致能力的“跷跷板”效应。作者还评估了教师难度过滤和学生动态抽样两种数据选择策略，后者在去除学生已掌握的问题后带来小幅但一致的提升。

methodology.title: 受控因素逐一变更
methodology.detail: 在保持其他条件不变的情况下，分别测试训练难度（教师通过率）、语言（English→Chinese）、推理跨度（短→长）、任务域（math、code、science）以及模型来源（同源 vs 跨源）的影响。

methodology.title: 教师难度过滤
methodology.detail: 根据教师在训练问题上的通过率，将完全未解（pass‑rate=0）或完全解出（pass‑rate=1）的样本单独保留，以评估难度对OPD的影响。

methodology.title: 学生动态抽样
methodology.detail: 在训练过程中动态丢弃学生已能正确解出的样本（pass‑rate∈[0,1)），比较三种抽样策略对最终性能的影响。

methodology.title: 多教师混合实验
methodology.detail: 在Multi‑Teacher OPD (MOPD) 设置下，改变不同教师的混合比例，观察学生在各领域的性能变化，验证“seesaw”效应。

mechanism.title: 推理行为迁移
mechanism.detail: OPD通过在学生实际访问的状态上向教师查询，实现对教师推理路径的模仿，而非单纯记忆教师的答案。

mechanism.title: 模型来源影响
mechanism.detail: 同源教师（与学生同一模型系列）在语言、推理深度和跨域上均能将学生拉近教师水平；跨源教师的迁移主要局限于训练分布内。

mechanism.title: 能力跷跷板效应
mechanism.detail: 在MOPD 中，路由到不同领域专家的提示仍会受到其他教师的隐式影响，混合比例的微调会在各领域能力之间产生相互拉扯。

experiments.title: 模型与数据
experiments.detail: 教师模型包括 Polaris‑7B、Light‑R1‑14B、JustRL‑1.5B、Nemotron‑1.5B；学生模型为 DS‑distill‑1.5B、DS‑distill‑7B。训练数据覆盖数学（BigMath、AMC2023、MATH500、AIME2025/2026、BeyondAIME、OlymMATH‑Hard）、代码（LiveCodeBench）和科学（GPQA‑Diamond）等多域。

experiments.title: 基线与对照
experiments.detail: 对照组为不使用任何过滤或动态抽样的标准OPD；实验组分别使用教师难度过滤（pass‑rate=0、=1）和学生动态抽样（保留已解、未解或丢弃已解）。

experiments.title: 评估指标
experiments.detail: 主要使用各基准的通过率/准确率百分比；跨域实验报告同源与跨源教师在目标域的相对提升幅度。

findings.title: 训练难度影响微弱
findings.detail: 教师未解的难题仍能提供约80% 的OPD增益，表明难度对同域泛化影响不大。

findings.title: 动态抽样带来小幅提升
findings.detail: 在六个数学基准上，丢弃学生已解问题的策略使平均性能提升0.6个百分点（+0.6 pp）。

findings.detail: 跨源配对在跨域任务上提升有限，往往只能匹配训练分布内的表现。

findings.title: 多教师混合产生seesaw效应
findings.detail: 改变教师混合比例会在不同领域的能力之间产生相互拉扯，导致性能在各域之间呈现“跷跷板”式波动。

contributions: 系统化的受控实验框架，逐一评估OPD在难度、语言、推理深度、任务域和模型来源上的泛化行为。
发现OPD主要迁移教师的推理模式，而非具体答案，且同源教师在跨域上具有显著优势。
提供教师难度过滤和学生动态抽样两种数据选择策略的实证评估，为OPD 的数据构建提供指导。
limitations: 实验仅覆盖7B/1.5B规模模型和数学、代码、科学等有限任务域，未验证更大模型或其他领域的可推广性。
缺乏对观察到的同源/跨源效应的理论解释，仅提供经验性描述。
未比较OPD 与其他离线蒸馏或RLHF 方法的相对优势。
open_questions: 在更大规模或不同架构的模型上，OPD 的推理行为迁移是否仍然成立？
能否构建理论模型解释模型来源对跨域迁移的影响机制？
如何设计教师混合策略以消除多教师设置中的能力跷跷板效应？
